title: OP Client Profile (authored)
description: The declarative half of an OP Client Profile. This file declares intent and pointers only; anything discoverable (named publishers, harmonizers) is resolved at init from the declared directories and surfaced via the resolved profile, never written here. Every field is optional unless noted; the loader fills documented defaults.

identity.description: Who this client is. Everything here is optional and identity-only — nothing operational. Consumers render what's present and skip what isn't (the 'OP Client card').

instance.description: Canonical base URL of this client. Authored here rather than .env (.env is secrets-only); a deploy-level environment override, when present, wins — see loader precedence notes. Required for a functioning client, but may be supplied entirely by the override (e.g. staging).

terms.description: Usable URI prefix for all terms on this instance — appending a term name yields that term's URI (and is how feeds.thorpes term names expand). Must match the prefix actually minted into the graph (currently instance + '~/'). NOTE: this key previously meant terms-of-service; that link needs a new home (rules?).

feeds.description: Known-shape feed pointers for building a rich client card: 'if you want to follow / embed / explore this relay, pay attention to these.' Keys are conventional slots. A value is either a URL (relative to instance or absolute) or an array of term names the consumer builds feed URLs from.

images.description: Identity imagery. All optional. Note: the registration badge is NOT identity — it lives at policies.access.badge.

contact.description: Freeform map of contact/follow points ({ email, bluesky, fediverse, ... }). This replaces the old externalAccounts field: discovery lives here; posting credentials live in .env, resolved at point-of-use by a posting publisher's own config.

policies.description: What this client will and won't do.

commercial.description: Whether this relay engages in / indexes commercial activity. A relay that indexes commercial activity is a commercial relay.

labels.description: Content labels. Reserved — rides on #192 via #270. Shape TBD there.

indexing.description: WHAT TRIGGERS indexing. Orthogonal to policies.access.registration, which governs WHAT GATE an index request must pass. All six combinations are valid.

mode.description: 'request' (default): indexing happens only when asked via /index. 'active': this client crawls/re-indexes on its own schedule. Maps to core's createClient({ config.indexingMode }) as the IDENTITY function — same two spellings, no translation table.

frequency.description: Re-index cadence when mode is 'active'. Inert under 'request'.

access.description: WHAT GATE an index request must pass. Orthogonal to policies.indexing.mode (what triggers indexing).

registration.description: The registration gate the indexing process enforces. 'registered' (default): the source origin must be verified in this client's datastore — today's behavior, the verifiedOrigin check in the indexer. 'open': no gate; any URL may be indexed (this is the ONLY mode in which blocks.domains is meaningful — allow all except listed; blocks.terms is separate and applies in every mode). 'closed': nothing is indexed unless its origin appears in whitelist.domains; a non-empty whitelist.domains is required or the relay can index nothing. NOTE: 'invite' was dropped from this enum — 'closed' plus a whitelist IS invite-only, and octothorp.es's own flow (submit form -> admin email -> admin approves) is just 'registered' with a human in the loop.

badge.description: Path to the badge image OP uses operationally (e.g. #168: badge triggers a registration request). Operational, not identity — identity imagery is identity.images.

blocks.description: Public blocklists, in two independent kinds with two DIFFERENT enforcement points. `domains` is the origin blocklist and is MEANINGFUL FOR THE INDEXING GATE ONLY when registration is 'open' (allow all except these) — enforced at the access gate in the indexing path. It is still consulted outside 'open' mode by the /register form's short-circuit, which checks it under every registration mode. `terms` is a term blocklist and is ORTHOGONAL TO THE REGISTRATION MODE: it applies under 'registered', 'open' and 'closed' alike, because a relay wants to refuse a slur term regardless of how its origin gate is configured; enforcement is at WRITE time during indexing, dropping the offending statement while the rest of the page indexes normally (the page is NOT rejected wholesale). Advertised deliberately; private blocks are the client's own business, rolled outside the profile. Validation guidance: a non-empty blocks.domains under any mode other than 'open' is a configuration error worth warning on — for the INDEXING GATE, 'registered' and 'closed' already exclude unlisted origins, so the list is inert there and misleadingly advertised (even though the /register form still consults it). blocks.terms carries NO such restriction and is never warned on. NOT RETROACTIVE: statements already written about a term that is later added to blocks.terms are not removed — retroactive removal is deletion work and belongs to epic #271. Read-time filtering (refusing to SERVE a blocked term's page) is deliberately not implemented; this is write-time only.

domains.description: Origin blocklist: either an inline array of strings, or a string path to a JSON file containing an array of strings. Blocklists get long and are often maintained separately, sometimes shared between deployments. The loader expands a path via an injected read dependency; a missing or unparseable file is a LOAD-TIME ERROR, not a silent empty list. The resolved profile always surfaces the expanded array, never the path.

terms.description: Term blocklist: same array-or-path form and same expansion rules as domains. Applies in ALL registration modes. A harmonized blobject carrying an octothorpe that names a blocked term has that statement dropped at write time; sibling statements on the same page still index.

whitelist.description: Public allowlist. MEANINGFUL ONLY when registration is 'closed' (index nothing except these), where it declares this relay's curated scope. Shaped as an object for symmetry with blocks, but carries `domains` ONLY: a terms allowlist is a different product decision with no current use case, so it is deliberately absent rather than reserved. Validation guidance: registration 'closed' with an empty whitelist.domains is a configuration error worth warning on — the relay can index nothing at all.

domains.description: Origin allowlist: either an inline array of strings, or a string path to a JSON file containing an array of strings, expanded by the loader exactly like blocks.domains.

api.description: What this client's API admits and exposes. linkTypes and documentRecord are authored declarations; publishers, handlers and harmonizers are POINTERS — the actual registries are resolved at init from the declared directories and appear only in the resolved profile. The three extension dirs are SIBLINGS, not nested: harmonizer definitions reference handlers through their `mode` field, so the dependency points harmonizer -> handler and nesting handlers under harmonizers would invert it. They are also different artifact kinds — handlers are JS modules exporting a function, harmonizers are declarative JSON ({ id, type, title, mode, schema: { subject: { ...selectors } } }) — so the same `dir` pattern is served by two different loaders: import modules vs read-and-validate JSON. A local harmonizer JSON file is the same shape as a harmonizer fetched over HTTP.

linkTypes.description: Declared first-class link types (formerly relationshipSubtypes, #236). Each mints a dedicated /get/<path>/<by> route; label feeds the generated vocabulary document. Undeclared types still work ad-hoc via ?st= (#200).

documentRecord.description: Admission + typing contract for document-record predicates (#237): what non-canonical metadata this client stores on index.

namespace.description: Short prefix resolved through core builtins plus vocabulary.namespaces.

iri.description: Explicit full predicate IRI; bypasses namespace resolution.

dir.description: Directory of site publishers. Init walks it and registers what it finds; discovered names appear in the resolved profile, never here.

named.description: Reserved: remote/additional publishers declared by reference ({ name, url }). Unioned with dir discovery at resolve time.

handlers.description: Content HANDLERS: JS modules exporting a harmonize function, registered by `mode` and by content-type. Sibling of harmonizers, not a child of it.

dir.description: Directory of site handler modules, walked at init like publishers.dir. Each module's default export is registered into the handler registry.

default.description: Default handler MODE when dispatch can't decide (explicit mode -> content-type -> this). Lives here, not under harmonizers: 'html' is a handler mode, not a harmonizer id — that category error is what this split fixes.

named.description: Reserved: remote/additional handlers by reference, unioned at resolve time.

harmonizers.description: HARMONIZERS: declarative JSON definitions ({ id, type, title, mode, schema }) that select fields out of a source. Each names the handler it runs under via `mode`, so handlers must be discoverable independently.

dir.description: Directory of site harmonizer definitions (.json), read and validated at init. Different loader from handlers.dir — these are data, not modules.

named.description: Reserved: remote harmonizers by reference, unioned at resolve time.

vocabulary.description: Namespace declarations for SPARQL and documentRecord resolution, and the identity of the OP vocabulary itself.

octo.description: The OP vocabulary namespace IRI. Defaults to the canonical vocabulary; override ONLY to use a forked or self-hosted vocabulary. Overriding is identity-affecting: different IRIs are written into the graph and your data no longer merges with standard-vocab relays. The resolved profile always surfaces the effective value.

namespaces.description: External namespaces this client operates with. Replaces core's hardcoded namespace map as the extension point; core still ships protocol builtins (octo, rdf, schema — foaf was audited as unused and demoted to declare-if-you-want-it).

import.description: false (default): declare-only — the prefix resolves in queries and documentRecord entries. true: init fetches the ontology and loads its triples into a named graph (Oxigraph does no inference; imported triples serve only queries that traverse them explicitly). Import implementation may ride with #270.

federation.description: RESERVED — post-v0.7 (candidate v0.8 main feature). Will hold replicate (dump/changefeed) first, query (read-only SPARQL passthrough tri-state) later. Declaring it now is a no-op.
